s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to broad-spectrum antibiotics, occurring in the context of recent immunotherapy
salient_findings: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
No clinical improvement with antibiotics or high-dose corticosteroids
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Recent treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab
Follow-up chest CT showed new bilateral infiltrative shadows
Patient reported fever and dyspnea
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative
Serologic testing for various autoantibodies was negative
No history of antigen exposure
No clinical improvement with lascufloxacin or tazobactam/ceftolozane
Oxygen requirement increased to 2 L/min and later to 4 L/min
No clinical improvement with high-dose corticosteroids
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages
CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy

shortlist.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent immunotherapy with ipilimumab and nivolumab, consistent with clinical presentation of bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to antibiotics

shortlist.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Exposure to various antigens can cause this condition, although no specific antigen exposure is mentioned, it remains a possibility given the patient's symptoms and lack of response to treatment

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Opportunistic infection that can occur in immunocompromised patients, such as those on immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to antibiotics, with negative serologic testing for various autoantibodies

shortlist.label: Acute interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe respiratory symptoms and bilateral infiltrative shadows, consistent with a diagnosis of acute interstitial pneumonia

raw.rationale: The patient's recent treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab, followed by the development of bilateral infiltrative shadows, fever, and dyspnea, is consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis. The lack of response to antibiotics and the presence of lymphocytosis in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid further support this diagnosis.

rejected.why: Sputum cultures and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and imaging are more consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis

rejected.label: Acute interstitial pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more specific to ICI-induced pneumonitis
